stem:
A 19-year-old man with cystic fibrosis has pancreatic exocrine insufficiency and loses weight despite eating well.

Enzyme replacement improves his protein digestion mainly by supplying which of the following?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Gastric products are being cast as pancreatic enzymes.
options.explanation: Pepsin begins gastric protein digestion and gastrin is a hormone; neither is supplied by pancreatic extracts, and gastric protein digestion is intact in this patient.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Carbohydrate-digesting enzymes are being used to fix protein digestion.
options.explanation: Amylase digests starch and lactase and sucrase are brush-border disaccharidases; none of them acts on proteins.

options.label: C
options.misconception: None; the pancreatic proteases digest protein in the small intestine.
options.explanation: The pancreas releases most of the digestive enzymes, including the proteases trypsin, chymotrypsin, and elastase, which cleave specific bonds in amino-acid sequences.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Fat-emulsifying agents are being cast as proteases.
options.explanation: Bile components emulsify lipids into micelles for absorption; they have no enzymatic activity and do not digest protein.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Lipid-digesting enzymes are being used to fix protein digestion.
options.explanation: Pancreatic lipases digest triglycerides and phospholipids; replacing them helps fat absorption but leaves defective protein digestion uncorrected.

context: Learning objective: the pancreas supplies most digestive enzymes. Proteases (trypsin, chymotrypsin, elastase) cleave proteins at specific peptide bonds; amylase digests starch; lipases digest fats. Exocrine insufficiency causes malabsorption treatable with enzyme replacement.
